issues.title: Keystone Core has restarted: Generation 1 is archived, Generation 2 begins
issues.body:
<!-- keystone-core-task: ANNOUNCE-reboot -->

**Keystone Core has restarted from a narrower base.**

In September 2026 the project accepted a reboot. The Generation 1 implementation — around 1,900 files, two public releases, a large feature surface — was archived rather than continued, and the repository now holds planning, governance and transition evidence. **There is nothing to install.**

### Why

Not because it failed to work. Because its breadth outran the evidence that any single operator journey worked end to end. Late fixes had found enrollment credentials that were not retained, and state and blueprint applies that did not reliably reach remote agents — cases where package-level test coverage sat alongside missing production wiring. Adding features would have preserved that risk rather than resolved it.

### Nothing was deleted

| | |
|---|---|
| Archive branch | `archive/2026-09-pre-v0.6-reboot` |
| Signed tag | `archive-2026-09-pre-v0.6-reboot` |
| Offline bundle | held by the maintainer, SHA-256 in the transition manifest |

Both refs are protected against update and deletion. The `v0.1.0` and `v0.5.0` releases remain published, with their artifacts intact, and are unsupported: they receive no updates, including security updates.

The 106 open Generation 1 issues were closed as **superseded, not completed** — closed because the project changed direction, not because the work was finished or judged unwanted. Their titles, bodies, comments, labels and milestones are retained.

### What Generation 2 is

One promise, deliberately narrow:

> An operator can securely enroll a Linux agent, target it, execute a bounded
> command over NATS, observe its durable lifecycle, cancel it, and retrieve an
> auditable result.

Nothing else ships until that is demonstrably true. State management, blueprints, runbooks, plugins, secrets, GitOps, webhooks, policy and clustering are Future candidates rather than commitments. Every capability Generation 1 had is catalogued with its status, known gaps and archived source, so the reboot discards the code without discarding what was learned.

### Where to read more

- [RFC 0001](https://codeberg.org/Spicer-Creek-Solutions-LLC/keystone-core/src/branch/main/docs/rfcs/0001-generation-2-reboot.md) — the decision, its reasoning, and the alternatives rejected
- [REBOOT-EXECUTION-PLAN.md](https://codeberg.org/Spicer-Creek-Solutions-LLC/keystone-core/src/branch/main/docs/project/REBOOT-EXECUTION-PLAN.md) — every task, in order
- [FUTURE-CAPABILITIES.md](https://codeberg.org/Spicer-Creek-Solutions-LLC/keystone-core/src/branch/main/docs/project/FUTURE-CAPABILITIES.md) — the archive capability catalog
- [VERSIONING.md](https://codeberg.org/Spicer-Creek-Solutions-LLC/keystone-core/src/branch/main/docs/project/VERSIONING.md) — what the version numbers now mean
- [docs/transition/](https://codeberg.org/Spicer-Creek-Solutions-LLC/keystone-core/src/branch/main/docs/transition/) — the archive manifest and the tracker-retirement record

This issue is a statement of record and is not work to be done. Questions and objections are welcome as comments.

_Created by `tools/transition publish` (reboot task R09)._

issues.title: v0.6.0 — release tracker
issues.body:
<!-- keystone-core-task: TRACKER-v0.6.0 -->

**Release tracker for `v0.6.0`** — the first completed Generation 2 release.

`v0.6.0` ships when one promise is demonstrably true:

> An operator can securely enroll a Linux agent, target it, execute a bounded
> command over NATS, observe its durable lifecycle, cancel it, and retrieve an
> auditable result.

Demonstrably true means a black-box test drives the production CLI or API, crosses the production transport, executes in the intended agent process, and verifies the externally observable effect. Package tests support development; they do not satisfy acceptance.

Nothing else is in scope. Everything Generation 1 had is catalogued as a Future candidate rather than a commitment, and reaches this milestone only through the promotion gate.

### Foundation workstreams

No implementation starts until all twelve are accepted. Each is a separate approval and pull request.

| Workstream | Must follow |
|---|---|
| `P00` — Product charter and canonical journeys | R10 |
| `P01` — Threat model | P00 |
| `P02` — NATS-native capability ADR | P01 |
| `P03` — Enrollment and identity ADR | P01, P02 |
| `P04` — Subject authorization ADR and executable policy | P02, P03 |
| `P05` — Versioned encrypted protocol ADR | P01–P04 |
| `P06` — Delivery and job lifecycle ADR | P02, P04, P05 |
| `P07` — Safe execution ADR | P00, P01 |
| `P08` — Persistence and audit ADR | P01, P06 |
| `P09` — Local operator API and authorization ADR | P00, P01 |
| `P10` — Acceptance-harness design | P02–P09 |
| `P11` — Repository skeleton and CI | P00–P10 |

### Then the behaviour stages

Stage C (`C01`–`C16`) turns the accepted design into the release. It has no issues yet and will not get them until Stage P is accepted: each behaviour workstream splits into an acceptance-contract task and an implementation task, worked by different agents.

- Every task, in order: [REBOOT-EXECUTION-PLAN.md](https://codeberg.org/Spicer-Creek-Solutions-LLC/keystone-core/src/branch/main/docs/project/REBOOT-EXECUTION-PLAN.md)
- Version policy: [VERSIONING.md](https://codeberg.org/Spicer-Creek-Solutions-LLC/keystone-core/src/branch/main/docs/project/VERSIONING.md)
- Roadmap: [ROADMAP.md](https://codeberg.org/Spicer-Creek-Solutions-LLC/keystone-core/src/branch/main/docs/project/ROADMAP.md)

_Created by `tools/transition publish` (reboot task R09)._

issues.title: P00 — Product charter and canonical journeys
issues.body:
<!-- keystone-core-task: P00 -->

**Task `P00` — Generation 2 workstream epic.**

Define target operator, fleet profile, problems, measurable success, explicit
non-goals, and exact CLI journeys for enroll, list/presence, run, status, output,
cancel, and audit. Record the 60–90 day external validation plan and business
evidence gate. Freeze the initial argv-only execution boundary from RFC 0001.

**Must follow:** R10

### This epic carries no leaf issues yet

An epic is a workstream, not a unit of work, and it has no acceptance criteria of its own. Leaf issues are created only once this workstream has a checked-in dossier and its plan has been approved — never in advance. The dossier must define depends-on task IDs and commit SHAs, allowed paths, exact outputs, applicable requirement IDs, acceptance cases with N/A rationale, validation commands, documentation changes, security reviewer, rollback, and handoff artifacts.

- Full text of this workstream: [REBOOT-EXECUTION-PLAN.md](https://codeberg.org/Spicer-Creek-Solutions-LLC/keystone-core/src/branch/main/docs/project/REBOOT-EXECUTION-PLAN.md) § Stage P

issues.title: P05 — Versioned encrypted protocol ADR
issues.body:
<!-- keystone-core-task: P05 -->

**Task `P05` — Generation 2 workstream epic.**

Define envelope canonicalization, version negotiation, job and correlation IDs,
signatures, recipient encryption, replay bounds, timestamps/nonces, headers,
payload and output limits, forward compatibility, test vectors, and error codes.
Headers contain only routing-safe metadata—never secrets or plaintext commands.
Classify enrollment, command, cancellation, result, lifecycle event, and presence
messages by signer, verifier, encryption recipient, replay key/window, maximum
size, durability, retention, headers, and accepted metadata leakage.

**Must follow:** P01–P04
